- If sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.7) and forecast is rising steadily, reduce forecast slope to avoid over-optimism.  
- If sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.3) and forecast is flat or rising, aggressively lower forecast to reflect bearish sentiment.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior day), model tends to overshoot — cap forecast increase to 5–7% max from prior day.  
- When true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., after 80+ price spike, price drops sharply), model often fails to adjust — reduce forecast by 3–5% for next period if sentiment is neutral or slightly negative.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated negative swings (e.g., 3+ consecutive negative sentiment), model tends to ignore trend — force forecast to align with recent low or mean of last 5–7 days.  
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome deviates >10% from 30d average of history, adjust forecast to reflect recent volatility — don’t assume smooth continuation.  
- If sentiment is high but price drops sharply (e.g., 5%+ drop from peak), model often fails to anticipate — reduce forecast by 2–4% for next period to account for sentiment mismatch.
